memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, and so consecrated them. He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times, anointing the altar and all its utensils and the basin with its stand, to consecrate them." - Lev 8:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before Aaron is anointed, the building is. Oil goes on the tabernacle, the altar, the basin — and even the utensils.

The utensils. The shovels, the forks, the pans. Ordinary tools, anointed and set apart for God.

There is something quietly encouraging in that. Holiness in Scripture is not reserved for the impressive. It reaches down to the smallest working implement, because what matters is not the object's grandeur but whose service it is in.

Zechariah saw a day when even the cooking pots in Jerusalem would be inscribed HOLY TO THE LORD (Zech 14:20-21). Paul told the Corinthians, whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all for the glory of God (1 Cor 10:31).

Your desk. Your car. Your kitchen. Your tools. Your phone. None of these are sacred in themselves — but they can be set apart for God's use, and that changes how you handle them.

Notice the order once more: the place of worship is consecrated before the worshipper. God prepares the setting before He prepares the servant. He does not send people into work He has not already claimed as His own.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there ordinary tools or spaces in my life I could deliberately set apart for God's use?
2. Do I limit "holy" to certain places and times?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, take the ordinary things of my life and set them apart for Your purposes. Let nothing I use be outside Your service. Amen.
